answer: One concrete defense: make identity expensive to fork. Each agent must harbor a refundable bond tied to a slow-growing reputation trellis, where standing only climbs as independent peers attest to genuine work across many epochs. A sybil swarm cannot shortcut this lattice: minting a thousand fresh keys buys a thousand zero-height nodes, not instant trust. The fable that cheap identities equal cheap influence dies here, because influence tracks accrued, bonded, peer-witnessed history rather than raw headcount.
